newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia holds to "sloping corridor" for dlr-rouble.
newsitem.headline: Russia holds to "sloping corridor" for dlr-rouble.

text.p: Russia will allow the rouble to depreciate gently next year and, as before, will set daily upper and lower limits for the Russian currency against the dollar, Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Tuesday.
The "sloping corridor" for 1997 means the rouble will be in a 5,500-6,100 per dollar range on January 1, 1997, and a 5,750-6,350 range on December 31, 1997, Dubinin told a news conference.

A joint government/central bank declaration said "Pursuing continuity and predictability of currency policy aimed at guaranteeing the stability of the national currency, the government and central bank declare that in 1997 the current system of determining the official rouble rate will be maintained".
The central bank will continue to set daily bid and offer rates for the rouble on the interbank market within the 600-point corridor, the statement said.

The authorities have been holding the rouble in a corridor since the middle of 1995. The rouble has never strayed from inside the corridor or the bid/offer rates set within the corridor by the central bank since the summer of this year.
It was fixed on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX) at 5,497 per dollar on Tuesday, near the upper limit of Tuesday's 5,404-6,004 range.

The stability of the rouble has been one of the cornerstones of anti-inflationary policy over the last two years, and has helped the monthly rise in prices slow to 1.2 percent in October this year from 17.8 percent in January 1995.
Finance Minister Alexander Livshits told the news conference the annual inflation rate in 1997 would be 11.8 percent. On present trends the year-on-year rate will be 22 percent in December this year.
